summary: Skill-point screen panel: a skill list (list widget + 51-entry id table), six embedded row-list groups for the skill rows, the party/point/change/renkei pane senders, a talk+yesno pair and the SP-cost display of the selected skill.
evidence: Ui_SkillPanel_InitPanes 0x0036D7C4 binds 'menu_skill_party', 'menu_skill_point', 'menu_skill_list', 'menu_skill_change', 'win_talk', 'win_yesno' and 'menu_skill_renkei'; Ui_SkillPanel_Ctor 0x0036F878 initialises the six row-list groups (see InitRowList 0x0036F6C8); Ui_SkillPanel_AddSpanEntry 0x0066EAFC / RemoveEntry 0x0022A9F8 maintain the 0x34-entry id table at +0x1D0 and the parallel pointer array at +0x100; SetSelectedIndex stores the list row. The embedded object chain also gives the class the Ui_PanelMessageWindow size (0x254C), so the class may share its layout with that window.

summary: Generic UI panel body: an owner/layout pointer, four (index, text-object) slots, two animation-reference lists, an inline array of eleven 0x50-byte sub-panels and a 16-word reset block. NOTE: struct_db grouped several unrelated recovered functions here (equip row, movie window, dungeon window, attribute panel), so this is a function family, not one proven class.
evidence: The class-level evidence is genuinely mixed: maybe_Ui_Panel_Ctor 0x003AA3AC builds the two animation-ref lists at +0x4C/+0x9C (released by Ui_NumberGridWindow_DeletingDtor 0x003AA3E0), Ui_Panel_SetFourTexts 0x001F044C uses the four (index,object) slot pairs at +0xC..+0x28, Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush 0x0019BD2C zeroes the 16-word block at +0x1120..+0x115C, while the dtor copies belong to Ui_EquipRow / MovieWindow / DungeonPlaceWindow. Field names therefore describe the strongest local evidence, with maybe_ wherever the owning function is only generic.
